projects.body:
Comodo SSL for a WordPress website

This technical demonstration by Md Arif Billah covers the connection between an SSL certificate, a Namecheap hosting account and a WordPress website. The documented scope includes certificate validation and installation, moving the website to HTTPS, and checking for mixed content. It is useful when reviewing how the hosting layer and application settings work together during an HTTPS setup.

What to review in the setup

  • Certificate validation and installation for the intended website domain.
  • WordPress address settings and the transition from HTTP to HTTPS.
  • Images, stylesheets and other page resources that still request an HTTP address.
  • Browser checks for certificate warnings, missing assets and unexpected redirects.

Installing a certificate and updating the website are related tasks, but they are not identical. A page can be reachable over HTTPS while some embedded resources still use insecure addresses. The distinction helps explain why checking a complete page matters in addition to confirming that the certificate is present.

Using the demonstration

Use the linked video to follow the demonstrated workflow and compare the relevant hosting and WordPress settings with your own environment. Certificate products, hosting interfaces and existing site configurations can differ, so domain-specific values should come from the account being configured. This entry documents a technical demonstration without claiming a named client deployment or measured security improvement.

Further reading: Namecheap's HTTPS guidance for WordPress.

projects.body:
Connecting a domain, hosting and WordPress

This HostGator setup walkthrough by Md Arif Billah brings together several tasks involved in preparing a WordPress website: accessing the hosting account, working with a domain, reviewing DNS configuration, installing WordPress and navigating cPanel. The scope is a practical introduction to how these parts fit together, rather than a comparison of hosting plans or a promise of a particular performance result.

What the walkthrough helps you identify

  • The hosting account and control panel used to manage the website environment.
  • The domain name visitors will use and the DNS settings that connect it to hosting.
  • The WordPress installation and the separate dashboard used to manage website content.
  • The relationship between hosting administration, website files and application access.

Keeping these roles clear makes the setup easier to understand. Registering a domain does not by itself install a website, and signing in to the hosting control panel is different from signing in to WordPress. The walkthrough provides a reference for recognizing those boundaries during a hosting setup.

Applying the overview to a website

Follow the linked demonstration with the details from the hosting account and domain you intend to use. Existing domains, email services and website installations can affect which changes are appropriate. The portfolio record describes the documented setup topics; it does not provide credentials, account-specific DNS values or evidence of a separate customer engagement.

projects.body:
WordPress deployment and file management in CyberPanel

This technical demonstration by Md Arif Billah covers two connected CyberPanel tasks: uploading website files and installing WordPress. Its documented scope includes creating or using the website workspace, managing files, preparing the database needed by WordPress and working with an OpenLiteSpeed hosting environment. The entry is useful for understanding how a hosting panel connects website administration with application deployment.

Files and application setup

  • Identify the website being managed before uploading or changing its files.
  • Understand the distinction between a website's document root and unrelated server folders.
  • Review database preparation and the application installation workflow for WordPress.
  • Check that the intended domain opens the expected website after deployment.

A WordPress website combines application files with database content. File management and installation therefore serve different purposes, even when both are accessible through the same control panel. Understanding that separation helps when following an installation, reviewing a deployment or organizing a later maintenance task.

Following the reference

The linked video is the demonstration reference for this entry. Use the hosting environment's own website names, file locations and database settings when comparing the workflow. Panel interfaces and installed components can vary. This portfolio page describes the supported subject matter without presenting the thumbnail as a screenshot of a named client's system.

Further reading: CyberPanel's WordPress deployment guide and website file manager documentation.

projects.body:
Email DNS for a cPanel-hosted domain

This technical demonstration by Md Arif Billah focuses on configuring email-related DNS records in Cloudflare for a domain using cPanel webmail. It covers MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC as distinct parts of a domain's email setup. The purpose is to make the role of each record clearer and show the relationship between the DNS provider and the hosting system that supplies email settings.

The records in this overview

  • MX records identify the mail service that receives email for the domain.
  • SPF records describe the systems authorized to send email for a domain.
  • DKIM publishes information used to verify email signatures.
  • DMARC communicates an authentication policy and can support reporting about email using the domain.

These records are related, but they do not replace one another. The correct values depend on the actual mail service and its configuration. Values shown in a demonstration should not be treated as settings for an unrelated domain. Review the records supplied by the hosting or email provider when applying the workflow.

Scope and demonstration reference

The linked video is specifically about Cloudflare DNS records for cPanel webmail. A separate portfolio overview also refers to this shared video; that does not establish an additional full mail-server deployment. Email authentication configuration is one part of operating email and does not guarantee inbox placement or a particular delivery rate.

Further reading: Cloudflare's DNS record type reference.
projects.description: Understand MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC record configuration in Cloudflare DNS for cPanel webmail, with an attributed video demonstration.

projects.body:
Hosting a static HTML website

This technical demonstration by Md Arif Billah covers deploying a raw HTML website on CyberPanel without installing a content management system. The documented scope includes placing website files in the intended document root, reviewing file permissions and working with the OpenLiteSpeed virtual host configuration associated with the website. It illustrates the relationship between static site files and the hosting environment that serves them.

What to check during deployment

  • The intended website and domain are selected in the hosting panel.
  • The HTML entry file and supporting styles, scripts and images are placed in the appropriate website folder.
  • Relative file references still point to the correct resources after the upload.
  • File access and virtual host settings allow the expected website to be served.

Static deployment has a different shape from a WordPress installation. The website can consist of ordinary files instead of an application backed by a content database. That makes file organization and resource paths especially visible when checking a deployment: a page may open while a missing stylesheet or image still needs attention.

Using this portfolio reference

Use the linked demonstration to understand the workflow, then compare it with the actual website folders and domain configuration in your own hosting account. This page describes a technical demonstration and its stated scope; it does not claim a named client launch, availability guarantee or measured hosting performance.

Further reading: CyberPanel website file manager documentation.
